objectives.description: command-structure.md -- per-site class decisions across 7 occurrences
objectives.note: This document's entire 'Command File Anatomy' worked example (frontmatter `command: plan`, the /plan usage string, the /plan status-validation sentence -- all inside one fenced code block, now lines ~38-206) is built on the premise that /plan is itself a standalone command file. That premise is stale (plan/research/implement are phases dispatched by /orchestrate, not command files), but the Non-Goals section forbids restructuring any document whose premise a dead command sits inside. Per that same section's guidance ('rewords the occurrences and records the residual incoherence'), a disclaimer was inserted immediately before the worked example (new lines ~30-34) stating plainly that /plan/research/implement are not runnable commands and that the example is illustrative of the general anatomy pattern still followed by live commands. The worked example's internal values were left untouched under that disclaimer rather than hand-edited piecemeal, which would have been a partial restructure. Outside the fenced example, four standalone 'Example:' lines (Pattern 1/2/5 illustrations and the two-vs-three-layer comparison diagram) were reworded individually to phase-dispatch framing: '/research 197' -> 'a research-phase dispatch for 197'; '/plan 196' -> 'a plan-phase dispatch for 196'; '/implement 259' -> 'an implement-phase dispatch for 259'; 'Route to /implement command' / 'Command File (/implement):' -> 'Route to the implement-phase dispatch' / 'Implement-Phase Dispatch:'. Class-1/2 judgment throughout; no class-3 sites in this file. Residual incoherence recorded: the document's title and 'Command File Anatomy' framing still treat /plan/research/implement as command files in spirit even with the disclaimer; a full restructure separating 'command files' from 'phase dispatch' is out of this task's Non-Goals and is named here as residue for a follow-up record, same as the core/docs/ scope-amendment precedent.
